provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: server.ts:294 exposes the 'ftp' directory publicly at /ftp, with directory listing turned on (serveIndex with icons: true). The only middleware in front of it is serveIndexMiddleware. Nothing in the Evidence shows that middleware checks who is logged in or what they are allowed to see. Its name and the vuln-code-snippet marker 'directoryListingChallenge' point to a challenge hook, not an access control. The data flow shows routes/order.ts:45 writing order PDFs straight into that same directory with fs.createWriteStream(path.join('ftp/', pdfFile)). These are per-customer order files tied to User records, which hold email (Contact data, models/user.ts), so any unauthenticated visitor can list and download other customers' order documents. This matches the positive example: a serveIndex directory with no auth check that a personal-data writer saves into. The negative example differs because it adds security.isAuthorized() and writes to a directory that isn't served. One gap: the Evidence doesn't include the PDF contents, so the claim that each file contains the customer's email is inferred from the order flow and the Contact category. This is a failure to control access to computer resources holding personal data.
